N03 — Trace-Barium SWRO: Selective Ba Removal Instead of Acid

A coastal-well SWRO plant operates at 70% recovery. Alkalinity is low, but trace Ba coexists with sulfate. Bulk Ca softening is costly, while a small chelating-resin guard bed is feasible. Use equilibrate_feed to identify the controlling mineral, test whether acid helps, and choose the lowest feasible Ba removal among 99%, 99.9% and 99.99% that meets Barite SI≤-0.10.

N03 — Stepwise Gold Answer: Trace-Barium SWRO: Selective Ba Removal Instead of Acid

The efficient reference trajectory uses 5 equilibrate_feed calls: zero-dose diagnosis, mechanism-based counterfactual pruning, then adjacent fail/pass points or a stated guarantee envelope to lock the stopping boundary. Other reasonable orders are acceptable if the information gain of each call is explained.

Key boundary check | Final conclusion

Recommend a Ba-selective chelating-resin guard bed that reduces Ba from 2.0×10^-4 to 2.0×10^-8 mol/s, or 99.99% removal. This yields Barite SI=-1.09786, Calcite SI=-0.51643, Gypsum SI=-0.09558 and pH=6.717. At 99.9% removal, Barite SI=-0.09787 still misses the -0.10 margin. HCl at 0.002 mol/s barely changes Barite SI (2.90186 to 2.90184) but drives pH to 3.727; acidification and bulk Ca softening therefore target the wrong mechanism.
